title: Contractual throughput admission and burst attenuator
author: Ethan Brooks
description: Introduce a contractual throughput admission controller and a burst attenuator to provide per-tenant guaranteed throughput while smoothing microbursts. Motivation: customers using Dedicated capacity require clear guarantees against noisy neighbors and predictable tail latencies during bursty traffic. This PR implements an admission layer that negotiates a tenant's committed throughput from their reservation metadata and enforces it via a tokenized admission queue plus a short-term burst attenuator that decays credits based on recent consumption. The change touches scheduler admission logic, the tenant reservation API, autoscaler signals, and telemetry. Key behaviors: 1) When a request arrives the admission controller checks committed_throughput and current_reserved_headroom; if within committed rate it admits immediately; if the tenant has burst credits the attenuator allows the request but debits burst_credits; if neither condition is met the request is queued behind guaranteed work and may be backpressured or overflowed to a secondary tier depending on policy. 2) Burst credits accumulate when a tenant consumes below committed throughput and decay with an exponential half-life when idle; a safety cap prevents unbounded credit accumulation. 3) The autoscaler receives a new metric (committed_utilization_ratio) that excludes transient burst-driven spikes so scaling decisions stay aligned to contractual load. 4) Rollout is opt-in per-tenant through a ReservationPolicy flag so we can pilot with a handful of customers before global rollout. This single commit description covers design, implementation, tests, docs, and migration notes. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked [x] Unit and integration tests [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated [x] Backwards-compatible API changes [x] Migration guide included. Related work: ENG-2148 (reservation contract schema), ENG-2201 (autoscaler signal filtering), SUP-587 (customer incident that motivated smoother admission).

review_conversation: Sofia Chen: Can we avoid an O(N) scan of tenant queues on every admission? Suggested using per-tenant token buckets attached to queue head.
Ethan Brooks: Switched to attaching a lightweight token bucket per queue head and added microbenchmarks showing <5% overhead at 95th percentile throughput.
Liam O'Connor: Autoscaler change looks good but please add a guard so committed_utilization_ratio is ignored for cold-start windows.
Ethan Brooks: Added cold-start window guard and unit test. Also added a Linear task to tune the window per workload.
Priya Rao: Telemetry names look noisy; prefer stable metric names to avoid dashboard churn.
Ethan Brooks: Normalized metric names and added deprecation warnings for legacy metrics; dashboards updated.
Infra CI: flaky integration on GPU runner; re-ran full test matrix and all checks passed.
ci_checks: benchmarks: microbenchmarks show 4.7% median overhead on 8k qps sample
release_notes: Add opt-in contractual throughput admission and burst attenuator. Provides per-tenant committed throughput enforcement and burst smoothing credits. Introduces metrics: redwood.reservation.committed_throughput, redwood.reservation.burst_credits, redwood.reservation.smoothing_violations, redwood.autoscaler.committed_utilization_ratio. Opt-in via ReservationPolicy flag; see docs/reservations/contractual-throughput.md for migration steps.
notes_for_operators: Default behavior unaffected until ReservationPolicy flag enabled. When enabling for production tenants start with low committed_throughput values and monitor smoothing_violations to tune decay half-life. Autoscaler tuning: set ignore_window_seconds for committed_utilization_ratio to match warmup profiles.
migration_guide: 1) Add committed_throughput field to tenant reservation objects (backfill optionally). 2) Enable ReservationPolicy.contractual_admission=false by default and flip per-tenant. 3) Monitor telemetry metrics for two weeks and iterate on decay settings. 4) Coordinate with SRE for autoscaler parameter rollout.
